references.text: Moses instructs the Israelites to explain the meaning of Passover to their children when they ask, reflecting the theme of passing knowledge from generation to generation.
Fathers shall tell their sons about the Lord's deeds when He brought them out of Egypt, an example of seeking wisdom from the previous generation.
Job encourages asking earlier generations and learning from the fathers' wisdom, which directly reflects the call in Deuteronomy.
The psalmist refers to what the fathers have told about God's deeds in days of old.
The psalmist thinks of days of old and years from distant times, reflecting the call to remember the days of the past.
What the fathers have told shall not be hidden from their children but passed on to coming generations concerning the Lord's deeds.
The psalmist remembers days of old and meditates on all God's works, reflecting the call to remember the days of the past.
The Lord calls the people to remember the former things from ancient times, for He is God and there is no other.
